query: The research left five open questions. Walk me through them one at a time, each with the files involved, options, and your recommendation.
Grill me on this idea for offline sync until we both understand it. One question per message, with the answer you would pick.
The critique raised three findings that are really undecided trade-offs. Settle them with me one by one before the plan changes.
Before a plan exists for the permissions rework, find the decisions we have not made yet and ask me about each in turn.
Present decision 1 of the queued open questions from the draft plan as a full brief and wait for my answer before the next.
I have a rough direction for the notification service. Interview me down the design tree and end with a summary of what we agreed.
Record my answers to the open questions with their nuance and give me the consolidated agreed direction at the end.
we keep going back and forth on where validation lives; settle that question and the ones that depend on it, one message each
We settled the six decisions. Write them up as a plan document with the skills an implementer has to consult.
Research the code paths and current library versions we need before planning rate limiting for packages/api. Keep it read-only and cite the evidence.
Red-team plans/cache-redesign.md in a fresh context and report concrete failure modes without editing it.
Turn the completed migration branch, its plan record, and the session logs into a suite of reusable skills we can replay onto main.
Revise this inline rollout plan from the six review comments, preserve unresolved feedback, and return the new plan inline.
The delegated run landed its last commit. Close the plan out: evidenced status per criterion, what is still blocked and by what, and the open decisions with owners.
The plan looks right to me. Record it as approved after a last sanity check.
Review pull request #418 for correctness, security issues, and maintainability, then draft inline comments.
rationale: Pull-request review has a separate owner
